Everything checked out. The booking engine is live and there is no closure notice. Address and coordinates match (Nominatim returns 1645 SW 9th St). The 10 rooms, the Miami Suite, and the free bikes (WSVN says four) are confirmed. Mr & Mrs Smith says there are 40+ artworks by Little Havana artists, and WSVN names Domino Park as a stone's throw away. I found no resort fee, so $160 is honestly tier 1. Two limits: I could not check the price myself (Google Travel would not render), and I did not check that rooms are free for Nov 20-24, only that nothing says the hotel is closed. Mr & Mrs Smith's from-$148 with tax fits the price but does not prove it. Taste: a new, art-filled 10-room hotel off Calle Ocho is a strong, non-generic pick.

The facts hold. Broken Shaker is open Thu-Sun from 5pm (Thu 5pm-12am, Fri-Sat 5pm-1am, Sun 5pm-11pm). The hotel says 1 block from the beach, the rooms page lists private rooms (King, Premium King Suite and others), and coordinates resolve to The Broken Shaker at 2727 Indian Creek Dr. The price note is the problem. The hotel FAQ adds a mandatory $35 resort fee plus 14% tax, and the bikes are paid for by that fee, so 'free bikes' overclaims. $185 + $35 = $220 before tax, which puts it in tier 2. The rule I used for this whole batch: tier = hotel-site rate + mandatory nightly fee, before tax. If you tier on the room rate alone, keep tier 1 but still add the fee to the note. I also dropped 'from $111 elsewhere' because I could not confirm it is a private room rather than a bunk. The price itself and availability are unverified.

reason: Three claims come from Michelin's write-up and are contradicted by the hotel or recent guests. (1) theMove's 'ocean-view patio or balcony': faena.com lists all four room types (Casa Queen, Casa King, Double Double, King Studio Suite) as City View. (2) 'Beach cabanas': the hotel's fee policy covers beach lounge chairs, umbrella and towel service. A Nov 2025 Tripadvisor review says you get unbranded chairs and umbrellas to carry to the public beach yourself, and other reviewers say the beach is across the street. (3) 'Beachside': Nominatim shows the hotel on the inland side of Collins, with a public parking lot and the boardwalk between it and the sand. Confirmed: the 1930 Spanish-style building (Michelin), the Faena District, a quiet setting (reviews), and that the hotel is open and taking bookings. Faena's policy page adds a $28 resort fee plus 14% tax, so $209 + $28 = $237, still tier 2. The price and availability are unverified.
